entries.name: Songkran
entries.capsule: Thai New Year, April 13 to 15: merit-making at the temple, water poured over elders' hands, family visits and water play.
entries.dateRule: April 13 to 15 each year, a fixed public holiday in Thailand. Minnesota's temple keeps it on or near April 13; the large public festival is held separately in May (see Minnesota Songkran Festival).

dates.source: Singapore Embassy in Bangkok, Thai public holiday list 2026; Human Resources Online 2026 list
Fixed date (April 13-15); 2027 holiday list not yet opened

entries.whatItMarks: The traditional Thai solar new year. The Tourism Authority of Thailand describes it as marked by merit-making, water-pouring rituals for elders and temple visits, and notes UNESCO recognition as intangible cultural heritage.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Wat Promwachirayan in St. Louis Park held a Songkran Day service on Sunday, April 13, 2025, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. The temple's first St. Louis Park open house, April 9, 2017, was also a Songkran celebration open to the whole community. The large public celebration is held in May as the Minnesota Songkran Festival.

entries.name: Minnesota Songkran Festival
entries.capsule: Free two-day Thai New Year festival each May: food, dance, Muay Thai, parades and a Buddhist alms offering; open to all.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by the Thai Cultural Council of Minnesota and Wat Promwachirayan; held on a mid- or late-May weekend since 2022.

entries.whatItMarks: A public celebration of Thai New Year, held in May in Minnesota, presented by organizers as a festival for all Southeast Asian and Asian American communities.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: First held May 28-29, 2022 in front of the State Capitol; May 27-28, 2023 at the Capitol; May 18-19, 2024 at the Capitol, with an alms offering, a Four Regions of Thailand parade, Muay Thai, a Loy Krathong lantern segment, a Baai Sri Su Kwan blessing parade, a papaya salad contest and a drag show, and an estimated 40,000 attendees by the Thai consulate's count; May 10-11, 2025 at the Capitol, opened by Thailand's ambassador with a governor's proclamation presented by Public Safety Commissioner Bob Jacobson. The 2026 edition was listed for Wat Promwachirayan in St. Louis Park, Saturday 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. and Sunday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.

entries.name: Makha Bucha
entries.capsule: Buddhist holy day at the full moon of the third lunar month; candle-lit processions and merit-making at temples.
entries.dateRule: Full moon of the third Thai lunar month (in a leap-month year, the fourth), usually February or March. The Minnesota temple holds it on a nearby weekend.

entries.name: Asanha Bucha and start of Buddhist Lent
entries.capsule: Holy day of the Buddha's first sermon, followed the next day by the start of the three-month rains retreat.
entries.dateRule: Asanha Bucha is the full moon of the eighth Thai lunar month (the second eighth month in a leap-month year), usually July; Khao Phansa begins the next day. The Minnesota temple observes both on a nearby weekend.

entries.name: End of Buddhist Lent and Kathina season
entries.capsule: End of the three-month rains retreat, followed by a month of Kathina ceremonies offering new robes to monks.
entries.dateRule: Ok Phansa is the full moon of the eleventh Thai lunar month, about three lunar months after Khao Phansa; Kathina ceremonies follow within one month and are scheduled by each temple. Projected dates are not confirmed.

entries.whatItMarks: The close of the monks' three-month rains retreat. Kathina is an offering of robes and supplies to monks after the retreat.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Wat Promwachirayan held Buddhist Lent Ending Day on Sunday, Oct. 12, 2025, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. A Royal Kathina ceremony was held there on Oct. 27, 2024, with Thailand's deputy consul-general, the Thai community and Friends of Thailand; Dr. Tatpicha Nunta was the main contributor and also donated to the Thai Arts and Culture School of Minnesota.

entries.name: Loy Krathong
entries.capsule: Full-moon night in November when people float small decorated offerings (krathong) on water.
entries.dateRule: Full moon of the twelfth Thai lunar month, usually November. Not a fixed date; sources differ by a day for 2026.

dates.source: Projected full moon of the twelfth lunar month; a travel guide (UME Travel) gives Nov. 25, 2026

A 'Loy Krathong - Festival of Lights and Lanterns' segment ran at 6 p.m. on May 18, 2024 at the Minnesota Songkran Festival, and Loy Krathong was the Thai Association of Minnesota's award-winning Festival of Nations exhibit theme in 2012.
